$comment: Single source of truth for the site's identity. Every generated file (sitemap, robots, llms.txt, schema, page <head> blocks) reads from here. NAP consistency is a top-3 local ranking factor — change a value HERE, never in a page.

nap.$comment: Confirmed by the owner. Must appear byte-identical on the site, Google Business Profile, and every directory. 'phoneDisplay' is what humans read; 'phoneE164' is what tel: links and schema use.

nap._todo: addressLocality is still null on purpose. The homepage FAQ asks 'Do you work with businesses outside Albany?' and the (541) area code fits Albany, so Albany OR is the likely base -- but it is an inference, not a confirmed fact, and a wrong locality is a NAP mismatch against Google Business Profile. Confirm it, then set it here. Until then the site claims only 'Based in Oregon' and the schema uses areaServed + addressRegion, which is correct for a service-area business.

serviceArea._todo: These four are named in the approved funnel blueprint and in the site footer. Dedicated /web-design-<city>-or/ pages are a strong local-SEO play, but each must be >60% unique copy with real local specifics -- see docs/SEO-PLAYBOOK.md section 2. Swapping only the city name produces doorway pages and gets penalised.

sameAs.$comment: ONLY verified profiles that are actually owned. An unverified or guessed URL here is a trust-signal violation (handbook §3.3 + §9). Empty is correct until each is live and claimed.

social.ogImageAlt: Willamette Web Design — websites that grow local businesses

pricing.$comment: From the approved funnel blueprint. Terms that touch billing start date, hard costs and the guarantee are still open -- see docs/BUILD-NOTES.md and the NEEDS_REVIEW callouts on /terms/.

forms.$comment: The free presence check form is the funnel's soft-conversion path. It is wired to Netlify Forms: Netlify detects the form in the deployed HTML and captures POSTs to '/', so there is no backend to run. It only works on a Netlify deploy — locally the POST fails and site.js shows the phone-number fallback, which is correct behaviour, not a bug.
forms._todo: Netlify does NOT email you by default. After the first deploy open Netlify > Forms > presence-check > Settings > Form notifications and add an email notification to info@willametteweb.com, then submit a real test and confirm it arrives. Until that is done the submissions are captured but nobody is told, which looks exactly like a working form and loses every lead. Set this flag to true once a test email has actually landed.

application.$comment: The 30-Day Program application at /apply/ and /es/apply/. Unlike the presence check, this does NOT post to Netlify Forms: it writes to Supabase through a Netlify Function holding the service-role key, which is how the rest of the platform already talks to that database. Netlify Forms is kept as a parallel backup so there is still an email alert and a dashboard copy -- see docs/APPLICATION-SETUP.md.

booking.$comment: Scheduling link for the discovery call, shown on the application confirmation page. Null means no booking CTA is rendered -- the page then says only that we reply within one business day, which is the honest version until a real calendar exists. Set url, then re-run scripts/build-apply.py. Recommendations are in docs/APPLICATION-SETUP.md.
